flawed_step: Step 3: Claim that planarity guarantees a Kempe component whose interchange eliminates one color from N(v). Planarity only rules out certain simultaneously disjoint Kempe paths with alternating endpoints; it does not guarantee such a component when one of the four colors occurs twice among the five neighbors. This is precisely where the attempted Kempe argument cannot be justified.
assessment_summary: Step 1 is valid: the neighbor-color multiplicities are 2,1,1,1. Step 2 is valid: if two singleton-colored neighbors lie in different components of their bichromatic subgraph, swapping the component containing one removes a color from N(v). The required existence assertion in Step 3 does not follow from planarity, so the proposed universal single-interchange conclusion is false.
